name: spring equinox

attributes.attribute: a day the Celts did not mark as a feast
a megalithic monument aligned to the sun

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The spring equinox is a calendar point. The Celts did not mark the equinoxes. On that day the day and the night are equal, but the Celts did not keep it. They kept the festivals that fall between the equinoxes and the solstices. These are Samhain, Imbolc, Beltane, and Lughnasa. Yet the equinox has a meaning to an older people. Some monuments face the sunrise and the fall of the year. The great tomb of Brú na Bóinne is aligned to the sun. The Celts left the festival, but the stones remember.
